turns.thought:
Yes — that would explain it. Airplane Mode disables all your phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so it will show no signal even though your line is now active again.

Please turn it off:
- **iPhone:** Open **Settings** → toggle **Airplane Mode** OFF. (Or swipe down from the top-right corner and tap the ✈️ icon so it's no longer highlighted/orange.)
- **Android:** Open **Settings** → **Network & internet** → toggle **Airplane mode** OFF. (Or swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the ✈️ tile so it's grayed out.)

Your line 555-123-2002 is confirmed **Active** on our end with a valid contract through 2026-12-31, and bill B1234321 shows **Paid**, so there are no remaining account-level blocks on service.

Turn Airplane Mode off and let me know what you see in the status bar afterward. I'd expect signal bars and a network indicator (5G/4G/LTE) to come back. If you're still showing "No Signal" after that, tell me and we'll keep troubleshooting.

**Good news on the account side:**
- Line **555-123-2002** (L1002): **Active**, suspension cleared
- Bill **B1234321**: **Paid**
- Contract valid through **2026-12-31**
- Device **Smartphone Pro Max** (D1002): activated and registered on the account
- Data usage: **8.7 GB of 15 GB** — well under your limit, so this is not a data cap issue

So the account and line are clean. That points to something on the device itself. Let's go through these one at a time:

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data back on.** Your status bar shows "Data Disabled," which is a separate setting from Airplane Mode.
- iPhone: **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data** → ON
- Android: **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Mobile data** → ON

**Step 2 — Check the SIM card.** A SIM that isn't seated properly will cause exactly this: no signal, no calls, no data.
- iPhone: **Settings → General → About** — if you see "No SIM" or a SIM error, the card needs reseating.
- Android: **Settings → About phone → SIM status**.
- Power the phone off, remove the SIM tray, reinsert the SIM firmly, power back on. If your phone uses an eSIM, confirm the eSIM profile is still active in settings.

**Step 3 — Check APN settings.** Incorrect APN settings will block cellular service and data even with a good signal.
- iPhone: **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Network**
- Android: **Settings → Network & internet → Access Point Names**
- If the APN field is blank or looks wrong, reset to default (Android: menu → **Reset to default**; iPhone: contact us to push updated settings). **Then reboot the phone** for the change to apply.

**Step 4 — Check network mode.** If your phone is locked to 2G/3G, it can struggle to register.
- iPhone: **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data** → select **5G On** or **LTE**
- Android: **Settings → Network & internet → Preferred network mode** → **5G/4G preferred**
- Reboot after changing this.

Start with Step 1 and Step 2, then reboot and check the status bar again. Tell me exactly what you see — signal bars, network type (5G/4G/LTE), and whether "Data Disabled" is gone — and we'll go from there.

If none of these restore service, I'll escalate you to our technical support team for hands-on assistance, since it may indicate a hardware or SIM provisioning issue I can't resolve from here.
